description: The plot illustrates the relationship between training loss and step number for several model types and sizes. The x-axis is labeled “Step” and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 440,000, with tick labels at intervals of 20,000. The x-axis label is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise. The y-axis is labeled “Train Loss” and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 0.85, with tick labels at intervals of 0.05. There are five lines displayed on the plot. The first line, representing “ChemBART Small 20M”, is red and solid; it begins at approximately 0.75 at a step of 0 and decreases to approximately 0.16 at a step of 440,000. The second line, representing “ChemBART Medium 20M”, is orange and solid; it begins at approximately 0.75 at a step of 0 and decreases to approximately 0.05 at a step of 440,000. The third line, representing “ChemBERTa Small 20M”, is green and solid; it begins at approximately 0.75 at a step of 0 and decreases to approximately 0.12 at a step of 440,000. The fourth line, representing “ChemLLaMA Small 20M”, is purple and solid; it begins at approximately 0.75 at a step of 0 and decreases to approximately 0.03 at a step of 440,000. The fifth line, representing “ChemLLaMA Medium 20M”, is brown and solid; it begins at approximately 0.75 at a step of 0 and decreases to approximately 0.01 at a step of 440,000.
caption_used: Training Loss vs. Steps for Each Model Type by Model Size with a Data Size of 20 million. The loss trends for 10 million and 20 million datasets are similar. The ChemBERTa Small 20M model exhibits the steepest decline in training loss, reaching approximately 0.15 at 440k steps. ChemLLaMA Medium 20M consistently outperforms ChemBART Medium 20M, achieving the lowest loss of all models at 0.01. The ChemBART Small 20M model shows a slower rate of decline compared to ChemLLaMA Small 20M, stabilizing at around 0.25 at 440k steps.
